title: Spike: map cpal playback time to the Link clock; varispeed bridge vs bar-line re-phase; drift trim
description:
## Intent
Answer M0 questions 3 and 5: how the `Mixer` should follow an outside clock.

## Steps (throwaway)
1. Map cpal's `OutputCallbackInfo::timestamp().playback` to the Link clock's microseconds; log the offset per callback for 10 minutes; report its jitter and drift.
2. Prototype two strategies on a copy of `crates/apricity-engine/src/mixer.rs` fed by a scripted clock:
   - **varispeed bridge**: after a tempo change, read the current `Arrangement` at rate `session tempo / rendered tempo` (linear or cubic interpolation) until the arrangement re-warped for the new tempo swaps in at the next bar line;
   - **hard re-phase**: keep the old rate and jump to the right frame at each bar line with the 5 ms crossfade (`XFADE`).
   Listen to both on a drum loop and a sustained pad at 120 to 90 BPM and at 120 to 123 BPM.
3. Drift: device clock vs Link clock. Measure the error without correction over 10 minutes; try a rate trim (at most ±0.1%) and a resync threshold (proposal: jump with a crossfade when the error exceeds 20 ms).
4. Estimate re-render time after a tempo change for `examples/march-blues.yaml` (every event re-renders; the cache key includes the tempo-dependent length).

## Leaves
A comment with measurements and a recommendation for each question, feeding `design/link.md` Decisions.

## Verify
The comment holds: offset jitter (ms), drift per 10 minutes, a listening verdict for each strategy, the chosen trim and threshold, re-render time.

Label `daw`. Commit: none (spike).
